verses.1: And in the twelfth year of King Yeroboam, son of Nebat, Abiyam became king over Judah.
verses.2: He ruled in Jerusalem for three years. His mother’s name was Maachah, daughter of Abishalom.
verses.3: And he followed in the footsteps of all the sins his father had committed. His heart was not pure before Jehovah, his God, just like the heart of David, his father.
verses.4: For David was given by Jehovah, his God, a city in Jerusalem, so that he could build his descendants there and establish Jerusalem as a city.
verses.5: For David did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah. He never failed to obey all that Jehovah commanded him throughout his life, only according to Urie’s instructions.
verses.6: And there was a war between Rehobam and Yaravham, all the days of their lives.
verses.7: And all the words of Abiram, and everything he did, are recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Judah. There was a war between Abiram and Jerubbaal.
verses.8: And Abiam slept with his fathers. They buried him in the city of David. And Asa, his son, became king after him.
verses.9: And in the forty-second year of King Jeroboam, king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.
verses.10: And in the forty-first year, he ruled in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Maakah, daughter of Abishalom.
verses.11: And Asa did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, just as his father David did.
verses.12: And the sacred objects were removed from the earth. All the idols that his ancestors had made were also destroyed.
verses.13: And he also cut off her head. He removed it from the pole that she had made from wood. And Noah burned her wooden statue in the river Kedar.
verses.14: And the promises were not broken. They remained true to Asa throughout his entire life.
verses.15: And he brought out the sacred objects of his father’s house, as well as the sacred objects from the Temple of Jehovah: gold, silver, and other precious items.
verses.16: And there was war between Asa and Baasha, king of Israel, all their days.
verses.17: And in the year 586 BC, King Israel attacked Judah. He built the wall to prevent anyone from entering or leaving. This was done by King Yehuada.
verses.18: And Asa took all the silver and gold that remained in the treasuries of the House of God, as well as the treasures of the king’s palace. He gave them to his servants. Then King Asa sent them to Hador, son of Tabrimon, son of Hagziion, king of Aram, who ruled in Damashk.
verses.19: A covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Now, I have sent to you gold and silver as a gift. This is to break your covenant with me. May this be a sign from God for the people of Israel.
verses.20: And Ben-Hadad heard of King Asa’s actions. He sent his soldiers to attack the cities of Israel. They captured Sion, Dan, and Avshal-Beth Maachah. They also destroyed all the shrines throughout the land of Naphtali.
verses.21: And when he heard the noise, he stopped building the tower. He sat down as he wished.
verses.22: And King Asa made all the Israelites clean. They took up the stones from the ruins and the branches that had been cut from them. With these stones, King Asa built the walls of Bethel and the Temple.
verses.23: And all the words of Assyria, and all its greatness, and everything it did, and all the cities it built—none of these are written in the record of the days of the kings of Judah. They were written only during his old age, when his feet became weak.
verses.24: And Asa lay down with his fathers. He was buried in the city of David, his father’s city. And Jehosaphat became his king.
verses.25: And Nadab, son of Jeroboam, became king over Israel during the second year of Asa, king of Judah. He ruled over Israel for two years.
verses.26: He did evil in the eyes of Jehovah. He followed in the footsteps of his father, and committed the same sins that he had led Israel to commit.
verses.27: And He set him over the house of Ishmael, his brother. He ruled over them from a lofty position, and all of Israel’s poor people also relied on his rule.
verses.28: And he died in the year three hundred of Asa, king of Judah. He was succeeded by another king.
verses.29: And as king, he destroyed every house of Jeroboam. He did not spare a single person from Jeroboam’s family; they were all killed according to Jehovah’s command, as spoken by his servant Ahia the Shiloni.
verses.30: For the sins of Jeroboam, who sinned and led Israel astray through his anger. He angered the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.31: And all the words of Nodab, and everything he did, are recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.32: And there was war between Asa and Baasha, king of Israel, all their days.
verses.33: In the third year of Asa, king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah ruled over all Israel. He ruled for forty-four years.
verses.34: He did evil in the eyes of Jehovah. He followed the ways of Jeroboam, and his sins led to the destruction of Israel.
